We need to generate new test cases for addRecord method covering other branches: SOA record with name matching origin, SOA record with mismatched origin (should throw), record with name not subdomain of origin (absolute not subdomain) throws, adding record when rrset does not exist (creates new RRset), adding record when rrset exists (adds to existing), adding SOA when rrset exists (replace existing SOA and update SOA field). Also test thread safety? Not needed.

We need to know dependencies: Name, Record, Type, RRset, SOARecord. We'll assume we can create mock objects or use real classes. Provide test case descriptions and input values as string representations.

We need to avoid duplication with Null Record test already present.

Thus produce groups: "SOA Owner Mismatch", "Record Not Subdomain", "Add New RRset", "Add Record to Existing RRset", "Replace Existing SOA". Possibly also "Add Non-SOA Record with Existing RRset". Provide inputs as parameter name r with value representation.

We'll output JSON array with groups.

Make sure format matches required: each case includes input list of objects with parameter and value (as string). expected: description of expected behavior (e.g., "IllegalArgumentException with message ...").

Let's craft.

We'll need to specify origin of zone; assume zone created with origin Name.fromString("example.com.").

Test case for SOA mismatch: r = new SOARecord(Name.fromString("other.com."), DClass.IN, 3600, ...). Expected IllegalArgumentException with message containing "SOA owner other.com. does not match zone origin example.com.".

Record not subdomain: r = new ARecord(Name.fromString("example.org."), DClass.IN, 3600, InetAddress.getByName("1.2.3.4")). Expected IllegalArgumentException with message containing "name example.org. is absolute and not a subdomain of example.com.".

Add new RRset: r = new ARecord(Name.fromString("www.example.com."), DClass.IN, 3600, ...). Expect zone contains RRset for name and type A, and no exception.

Add record to existing RRset: first add A record, then add another A record same name. Expect RRset contains both records.

Replace existing SOA: zone initially has SOA record; then add new SOA record with same origin. Expect old SOA removed, zone.SOA updated to new.

We need to express expected as maybe "no exception, RRset added" etc.

Let's produce JSON.
